title: Why Do Houseplants Tilt Toward Light?

scenes.text: Ever notice a potted fern leaning toward the window?
Most people think plants just grow where they get the most sunlight.
scenes.label: Plants grow only where sun hits
scenes.query: common belief plants need direct sun only
scenes.query2: myth plants grow only in light

scenes.text: In fact, plants actively bend toward light through phototropism, using the hormone auxin to grow longer on the darker side.
scenes.label: Phototropism uses auxin

scenes.text: So the tilt is a growth response, not just a random habit.
scenes.label: Growth Response
scenes.sub: Plants steer themselves toward brighter spots
scenes.query: plant bending toward light time lapse

scenes.text: Follow if you love learning something new.
scenes.query: nature facts short video end screen

description: Houseplants aren’t lazy – they use a clever hormone trick to chase the sun. Discover the science behind that daily lean and why it matters for your green friends.
